files.content: '''A kitchen-table mini-adventure about borrowed biscuit cutters and sharing.'''

# The Last Dough

At five o’clock the kitchen was so busy that the kettle had to wait for a clear patch of counter. Mum stirred soup with one hand and answered the phone with the other. A tray of cooling buns occupied the table. Mara and her younger brother, Eli, had been told not to get underfoot, which was difficult when the last bowl of biscuit dough sat exactly between them.

“Mrs. Flores lent us her cutters,” Mara said, eyeing the star and bell shapes in a picture she had drawn on a scrap of paper. “We should make her a thank-you gift. A proper one.”

Eli scraped a bit of flour off his sleeve. “We should make biscuits we can eat, too. We both kneaded that dough.”

“It’s the last of it,” Mum called over the soup pot. “And I need this counter in ten minutes. Decide what you’re making, then clean up after yourselves.” She sounded brisk, not cross. Still, the warning made the dough feel suddenly smaller.

Mrs. Flores lived next door. She had lent them her old metal cutters that morning after Mara explained she wanted to make a surprise for her. They were narrow at the edges, with a little bent handle on the star. Mara had promised to bring them back clean. Eli had come along because he was good at remembering promises, though he said that wasn’t why.

Mara lifted the bowl. “We can ask if she’s home and borrow them now.”

“You already asked,” Eli said. “She said yes. That’s what lending means.”

Mara smiled despite herself. They hurried next door, knocked, and heard a chair scrape. Mrs. Flores opened the door with flour on her cheek. “You’re right on time,” she said. “I was wondering what you’d make with those.” She handed them the star and bell cutters in a tea towel. “Bring them back dry. I may bake tonight.”

Back in the kitchen, Mum had moved the bowl to a cooler corner. The dough was soft from being left near the stove. A jar of flour stood open beside it, but the counter was cluttered with Mum’s chopping board and a stack of clean plates. Mara found a narrow space and dusted it carefully.

Eli watched her. “You’re using all the clear space for the gift.”

“I’m using enough space to make it look nice.”

“And what do I get?”

“You get to help.”

“That isn’t a biscuit.” Eli’s voice was quiet, which made Mara look up. He had kneaded the dough while she drew the card. He wasn’t trying to spoil the surprise. He didn’t want their work to disappear into a box without either of them getting a say.

Mara’s first answer was ready: Mrs. Flores had helped them, and thank-you gifts should be generous. But Eli rubbed the small patch of flour on his sleeve, and she remembered their grandmother letting each child press a cutter into dough before she divided the tray. The cookies had never been identical. The sharing had been.

“We can measure it,” Mara said. “Exactly half for you and half for me.”

Eli frowned. “Then how does the gift get any?”

“Each of us gives half of our half. The gift gets the same amount from both of us. We keep the other half to share.”

He considered this. “And if one side is bigger?”

“Then we fix it.”

They split the last dough on the kitchen scale. The needle wavered, and Eli steadied the bowl while Mara pinched off a little piece. Once the two portions matched, each took half of theirs for the gift. Mum cleared a strip of counter without stopping her soup. “That looks fair,” she said, and set the oven to warm.

The dough was still soft. Mara sprinkled flour over the counter and Eli dusted the cutters. Their first star came away clean; the second held on to one point until Eli loosened it with a fingertip. They cut bells too. One bell leaned sideways, and Mara started to remake it, but Eli said, “It still rings in somebody’s head.” She let it stay.

While the oven warmed, Eli tapped a rhythm on the table with a wooden spoon. Mara joined in with the tea tin, softer so Mum could hear the timer. Their kitchen song had no words until Eli announced, “Flour on the table, bell in the tin.” Mara added, “Two good bakers, one small win.” They laughed and stopped before the timer rang.

The biscuits browned at their edges. One star lost a point, and a bell puffed until it looked like a mitten. Mara’s face tightened. Eli broke off a tiny browned corner and tasted it. “Still a biscuit,” he said. “Still a thank-you.” Mara tried one too. It was warm and sweet, even if it wasn’t the perfect row she had imagined.

They chose the two neatest stars and the straighter bells for Mrs. Flores. The rest went onto a plate for them. Mara folded the scrap of paper into a card, and Eli wrote the words because his letters were bigger: THANK YOU FOR LENDING THE CUTTERS. They tucked the biscuits into a small tin lined with clean paper. The gift was modest, but every piece had been made by both of them.

Before leaving, they washed the cutters together. Dough clung to the star’s bent handle, so Eli worked it loose with a soft brush while Mara dried each shape with a towel. She checked the edges before wrapping them. “They’ll be ready for her batch,” she said. Eli nodded, pleased that returning them properly was part of the gift too.

They split one warm biscuit at the counter, exactly down its middle. Mum glanced over her shoulder. “You saved me a crumb?” Eli placed a small piece beside the soup. “For quality control.” Mum laughed and ate it.

Next door, Mrs. Flores opened the tin and read the card. She turned the crooked bell in her hand. “This one’s my favorite,” she said. “It looks like it’s dancing.” Mara’s shoulders dropped. Eli grinned at her, but didn’t say he had been right. He didn’t need to.

Mara gave back the clean, dry cutters. Mrs. Flores set them beside a bowl of dough she had already prepared for her own evening baking. “Let’s see if your star still works,” she said, pressing it into the dough. It cut a clean shape. The borrowed tool had come home useful, not merely returned.

At the doorway, Mara thanked her for lending it. Eli thanked her for waiting while they made the card. On the walk back, neither carried the tin. It was empty, and that was how they knew the gift had reached its destination. In the kitchen, the last dough was gone, but their half of the promise had been kept together.

def render(scene_id, params, before, after):
    if scene_id == 'start':
        return ('Steam fogged the kitchen window while Mum steered a soup pot around the cooling rack. '
                'Mara spotted the last bowl of biscuit dough. “Mrs. Flores lent us her cutters,” she said. '
                '“We can make her a thank-you box.” Eli wiped flour from his nose. “If we split the dough fairly.”')
    if scene_id == 'borrow_cutters':
        condition = ('The star’s bent edge was tacky, so they washed it before carrying it home. '
                     if before['cutters.tacky'] else
                     'The metal was already clean; Eli dried it carefully before they carried it home. ')
        return ('Mara and Eli went next door and asked Mrs. Flores for the star and bell cutters. '
                '“Of course,” she said. “I may bake tonight, so bring them back dry.” '
                + condition + 'Back in their crowded kitchen, the borrowed shapes waited beside the last dough.')
    if scene_id == 'flour_memory':
        return ('Eli dusted a clean patch of counter, then remembered their grandmother letting both children '
                'press cutters into dough. “She never cared if the stars matched,” he said. Mara smiled. '
                '“She cared that we both got a turn.” The memory softened Eli’s voice before either of them '
                'had to argue about the bowl.')
    if scene_id == 'timer_song':
        return ('With the oven warming, Eli tapped a rhythm on the table with a wooden spoon. Mara answered '
                'on the tea tin, quietly enough not to drown Mum’s timer. “Flour on the table, bell in the tin,” '
                'Eli sang. Mara added a rhyme about two good bakers. Their silly song made the wait feel shorter.')
    if scene_id == 'prepare_dough':
        surface = ('Mara dusted the narrow counter with the flour Mum had left out. ' if after['dough.floured']
                   else 'The chilled dough felt firm, though there was no spare flour for the counter. ')
        oven = ('The oven was already warming. ' if before['oven.preheated']
                else 'Mara turned on the oven and waited for it to warm. ')
        texture = ('The dough held its edge when Eli pressed it; they could make neat shapes. '
                   if after['dough.quality'] == 'neat' else
                   'The warm dough clung to their fingers; without flour, clean shapes would be difficult. ')
        return ('Mara brought the last dough to the clear strip of counter. ' + surface + oven + texture
                + 'Eli looked at the small bowl. “That’s all of it,” he said. Neither could count on another batch.')
    if scene_id == 'divide_dough':
        if after['share.plan'] == 'equal':
            callback = ('Eli remembered the old shared trays and relaxed. ' if before['memory.shared'] else '')
            return ('“Half for you, half for me,” Eli said. Mara frowned. “And Mrs. Flores?” '
                    'They weighed the portions, then each set aside an equal part for the thank-you tin. '
                    + callback + 'The rest stayed for their own plate. “If one side is bigger, we fix it,” Mara said. '
                    'Eli steadied the bowl until the scale settled.')
        return ('“The gift should get the larger part,” Mara said. Eli watched her divide the dough. '
                '“Then we share what’s left exactly.” She stopped, listened, and measured again. '
                'They agreed together to send most of the dough next door and keep a smaller piece for themselves. '
                'The choice was generous, but it left no doubt about who had agreed to it.')
    if scene_id == 'bake':
        if after['cookies.gift_ready']:
            song = 'Their timer song kept time while the tray browned. ' if before['kitchen.timer_song'] else ''
            return (song + 'The borrowed star and bell cutters lifted cleanly from the dough. In the oven, '
                    'the edges turned gold. One star lost a point, but the gift portion held together. '
                    'Mara set aside the neat shapes for Mrs. Flores; Eli rescued the smaller home biscuit. '
                    'The cutters came out smeared with dough.')
        reason = ('The warm dough stuck without flour, and the shapes slumped in the oven. '
                  if after['dough.quality'] == 'rough' else
                  'There was too little dough in the gift portion for a proper box of shapes. ')
        return (reason + 'The biscuits still smelled sweet, but none would travel neatly as a gift. '
                'Mara watched a star lose its points. Eli nudged the crumbs into a little pile. '
                '“We can tell her what happened,” he said. The tray was edible, if not what they had planned.')
    if scene_id == 'wrap_box':
        if after['gift.status'] == 'boxed':
            return ('Mara wrote a thank-you card while Eli lined a small tin with clean paper. '
                    'They chose the neatest stars and bells for Mrs. Flores, leaving a little biscuit for home. '
                    'Then dough came off the borrowed cutters under warm water. Eli dried the bent star, '
                    'and Mara checked its edge. The tin and the tools were both ready for the visit.')
        return ('Mara wrote a thank-you card instead of pretending the misshapen biscuits were a present. '
                'Eli folded the note carefully. They would explain that the last dough had gone wrong, and '
                'still say thank you for the loan. After washing and drying the cutters, Mara tested the star '
                'with her thumb. It was clean and ready to work again.')
    if scene_id == 'ending_gift':
        plan = ('They explained that each had given the same amount to the tin. '
                if before['share.plan'] == 'equal' else
                'They explained that they had chosen to give most of the dough to her. ')
        return ('At Mrs. Flores’s kitchen, Mara offered the biscuit tin and Eli held out the card. '
                + plan + 'Mrs. Flores read it, chose the crooked bell as her favorite, and thanked them both. '
                'The siblings split their small home biscuit before leaving. They returned the clean cutters, '
                'and Mrs. Flores pressed the star into dough she had ready for her own baking. It cut cleanly.')
    if scene_id == 'ending_note':
        reason = ('They told Mrs. Flores the warm dough had stuck and the shapes had slumped. '
                  if before['dough.quality'] == 'rough' else
                  'They told Mrs. Flores there had not been enough dough left for a neat gift portion. ')
        return ('At Mrs. Flores’s kitchen, Eli gave her the thank-you note. ' + reason
                + 'She listened without pretending the biscuits were a success. The siblings shared the edible '
                'crumbs, then returned the clean, dry cutters. Mrs. Flores pressed the star into dough she had '
                'ready for her own baking. It cut cleanly. Their thanks had arrived, even without a perfect tin.')
    raise ValueError(f'no prose for scene {scene_id}')

from copy import deepcopy
from dataclasses import asdict, replace
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import unittest

from storyscenes.runtime import StoryError
from storyscenes.mini_adventures.kite.world import (
    Parameters, SCENES, generate, guard, initial, play_scene, replay, validate,
)


class KitchenAdventureTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def assert_row_replays(self, row):
        params = Parameters(**row['parameters'])
        episodes = replay(params, row['path'])
        self.assertEqual([asdict(e) | {'events': list(e.events)} for e in episodes], row['episodes'])
        self.assertEqual((chr(10) * 2).join(e.text for e in episodes), row['story'])
        self.assertEqual(episodes[-1].after, row['final_state'])
        self.assertTrue(row['final_state']['story.ended'])
        self.assertTrue(row['final_state']['story.outcome'])
        self.assertEqual(len(row['path']), row['scene_count'])
        self.assertEqual(len(row['path']), len(set(row['path'])))
        state = initial(params)
        for episode in episodes:
            self.assertEqual(state, episode.before)
            self.assertTrue(guard(episode.id, state))
            self.assertTrue(40 <= len(episode.text.split()) <= 70)
            self.assertTrue(episode.events)
            for event in episode.events:
                self.assertTrue(event['changes'])
                for key, value in event['requires'].items():
                    self.assertEqual(state[key], value)
                for key, values in event['changes'].items():
                    self.assertEqual(state[key], values['before'])
                    self.assertNotEqual(values['before'], values['after'])
                    state[key] = values['after']
                validate(state)
            self.assertEqual(state, episode.after)
        json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False)

    def test_both_lengths_over_one_hundred_seeds_and_exact_replay(self):
        for count in (7, 8):
            for seed in range(100):
                with self.subTest(count=count, seed=seed):
                    row = generate(seed, count=count)
                    self.assert_row_replays(row)
                    self.assertEqual(len(row['path']), count)
                    self.assertEqual(set(row['path']) & {'ending_gift', 'ending_note'},
                                     {row['path'][-1]})

    def test_optional_vignettes_are_selected_not_silently_applied(self):
        for seed in range(20):
            seven = generate(seed, count=7)
            eight = generate(seed, count=8)
            seven_vignettes = set(seven['path']) & {'flour_memory', 'timer_song'}
            eight_vignettes = set(eight['path']) & {'flour_memory', 'timer_song'}
            self.assertFalse(seven_vignettes)
            self.assertEqual(len(eight_vignettes), 1)
            state7 = seven['final_state']
            if 'flour_memory' not in seven['path']:
                self.assertFalse(state7['memory.shared'])
            if 'timer_song' not in seven['path']:
                self.assertFalse(state7['kitchen.timer_song'])

    def test_parameter_validation_is_strict(self):
        for kwargs in (
            {'dough_grams': True}, {'dough_grams': 69}, {'dough_grams': 181},
            {'dough_chilled': 1}, {'flour_available': 'yes'},
            {'cutters_tacky': 0}, {'oven_preheated': None}, {'share_plan': 'mostly'},
        ):
            with self.subTest(kwargs=kwargs), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                Parameters(**kwargs)
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            Parameters(100)
        for count in (True, 6, 9):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                generate(count=count)

    def test_illegal_scenes_and_actions_do_not_mutate_caller(self):
        params = Parameters()
        state = initial(params)
        saved = deepcopy(state)
        with self.assertRaises(StoryError):
            play_scene(params, state, 'bake')
        self.assertEqual(state, saved)
        first = play_scene(params, state, 'start')
        self.assertEqual(state, saved)
        local = __import__('storyscenes.mini_adventures.local_play', fromlist=['LocalPlay']).LocalPlay(
            initial(params), actors=('mara', 'eli'), validate=validate)
        before_state, before_events = deepcopy(local.state), deepcopy(local.events)
        with self.assertRaises(StoryError):
            local.act('illegal', requires={'dough.prepared': True}, **{'dough.grams': 90})
        self.assertEqual(local.state, before_state)
        self.assertEqual(local.events, before_events)
        self.assertEqual(first.before, saved)

    def test_cutters_and_dough_have_continuous_physical_state(self):
        params = Parameters(dough_grams=140, dough_chilled=True, flour_available=True,
                           cutters_tacky=True, oven_preheated=False, share_plan='equal')
        row = generate(13, count=7, params=params)
        state = initial(params)
        for episode in replay(params, row['path']):
            if episode.id == 'borrow_cutters':
                self.assertEqual(episode.after['cutters.carrier'], 'siblings')
                self.assertEqual(episode.after['cutters.location'], 'family_counter')
                self.assertTrue(episode.after['cutters.clean'])
            if episode.id == 'wrap_box':
                self.assertTrue(episode.after['cutters.ready'])
                self.assertEqual(episode.after['cutters.carrier'], 'siblings')
            state = episode.after
        final = row['final_state']
        self.assertEqual(final['cutters.owner'], 'Mrs Flores')
        self.assertEqual(final['cutters.carrier'], 'Mrs Flores')
        self.assertEqual(final['cutters.location'], 'neighbor_counter')
        self.assertTrue(final['cutters.returned'] and final['neighbor.cutter_used'])
        self.assertEqual(final['dough.for_gift'] + final['dough.for_home'], final['dough.grams'])

    def test_paired_counterfactuals_change_both_choice_and_ending(self):
        good = Parameters(dough_grams=140, dough_chilled=True, flour_available=True,
                          cutters_tacky=False, oven_preheated=True, share_plan='gift_first')
        bad = replace(good, dough_grams=80, dough_chilled=False, flour_available=False,
                      share_plan='equal')
        successful = generate(4, count=7, params=good)
        fallback = generate(4, count=7, params=bad)
        self.assertEqual(successful['path'][-1], 'ending_gift')
        self.assertEqual(fallback['path'][-1], 'ending_note')
        self.assertNotEqual(successful['final_state']['story.outcome'], fallback['final_state']['story.outcome'])
        equal = generate(4, count=7, params=replace(good, share_plan='equal'))
        self.assertNotEqual(successful['final_state']['dough.for_gift'], equal['final_state']['dough.for_gift'])
        self.assertEqual(successful['path'][:-1], equal['path'][:-1])

    def test_vignette_effects_are_persistent_and_path_specific(self):
        params = Parameters()
        base_path = ('start', 'borrow_cutters', 'prepare_dough', 'divide_dough', 'bake', 'wrap_box', 'ending_gift')
        base = replay(params, base_path)[-1].after
        with_memory = replay(params, ('start', 'borrow_cutters', 'flour_memory', 'prepare_dough',
                                      'divide_dough', 'bake', 'wrap_box', 'ending_gift'))[-1].after
        self.assertFalse(base['memory.shared'])
        self.assertTrue(with_memory['memory.shared'])
        self.assertGreater(with_memory['siblings.trust'], base['siblings.trust'])
        with_song = replay(params, ('start', 'borrow_cutters', 'prepare_dough', 'timer_song',
                                    'divide_dough', 'bake', 'wrap_box', 'ending_gift'))[-1].after
        self.assertTrue(with_song['kitchen.timer_song'])
        self.assertFalse(base['kitchen.timer_song'])

    def test_seeded_parameters_and_cli(self):
        self.assertEqual(Parameters(**asdict(__import__(
            'storyscenes.mini_adventures.kite.world', fromlist=['parameters']).parameters(9))),
            __import__('storyscenes.mini_adventures.kite.world', fromlist=['parameters']).parameters(9))
        result = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, '-m', 'storyscenes.mini_adventures.kite.world', '--seed', '0', '--scenes', '8'],
            capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
        self.assertTrue(result.stdout.strip())

# The Last Dough

A standard-library-only mini-adventure in a crowded family kitchen. Mara and Eli borrow their neighbor’s biscuit cutters to make a thank-you gift, then decide what to do with the last dough. The pack uses the supplied `LocalPlay` helper for guarded, atomic local actions and traces; it does not modify shared files or use a runtime language model.

## Run it

From the repository root:

```bash
python -m storyscenes.mini_adventures.kite.world --seed 0 --scenes 8
python -m storyscenes.mini_adventures.kite.world --seed 12 --scenes 7
python -m unittest storyscenes.mini_adventures.kite.test_world
python check_pack.py .
```

The program supports exactly seven or eight scenes. Seven-scene routes contain the six required encounters plus an ending. Eight-scene routes include exactly one optional vignette: `flour_memory` or `timer_song`. `generate` returns JSON-native parameters, the path, episode states and traces, complete prose, final state, and a bounded-search attempt count. `replay(params, path)` re-enacts the route.

You may override parameters from the command line with a JSON object:

```bash
python -m storyscenes.mini_adventures.kite.world --seed 0 --scenes 7 --params '{"dough_grams":140,"dough_chilled":true,"flour_available":true,"cutters_tacky":true,"oven_preheated":false,"share_plan":"equal"}'
```

The Python API is also convenient for reproducible recipes:

```python
from storyscenes.mini_adventures.kite.world import Parameters, generate

success = Parameters(dough_grams=140, dough_chilled=True, flour_available=True,
                     cutters_tacky=True, oven_preheated=False, share_plan='gift_first')
row = generate(2026102421, count=7, params=success)
print(row['path'][-1])  # ending_gift

fallback = Parameters(dough_grams=80, dough_chilled=False, flour_available=False,
                      cutters_tacky=False, oven_preheated=True, share_plan='equal')
row = generate(2026102421, count=8, params=fallback)
print(row['path'][-1])  # ending_note
```

These recipes explicitly select the outcomes. `ending_gift` requires neat shapes and at least 60 grams assigned to the gift. Either sharing plan can earn it: `gift_first` assigns two thirds of the dough to the gift; `equal` assigns half, with equal contributions from both siblings. The second recipe makes rough shapes and assigns too little dough to the gift, so the siblings deliver an honest note instead. In both endings they return clean cutters and Mrs. Flores uses them on her own dough.

## Parameters and consequences

`Parameters` is keyword-only and validates every value. `dough_grams` is an integer from 70 to 180. `dough_chilled`, `flour_available`, `cutters_tacky`, and `oven_preheated` must be booleans. `share_plan` is either `equal` or `gift_first`.

The dough is cut neatly if it is chilled or the counter can be floured; otherwise the warm dough smudges. Tacky cutters are washed before use. An unheated oven is preheated during preparation; light is not a prerequisite for heating. The dough is conserved across gift and home portions. The sharing plan changes those portions, while dough condition and amount determine which ending is possible. The borrowed cutters change carrier and location, become dirty through use, are washed, returned, and used by their owner.

## Limitations

This is a deliberately small scenario model, not a general kitchen physics engine. Dough quality is a two-state abstraction, oven behavior is limited to preheating, and the gift threshold is authored for this story. The siblings and recipient are fixed characters. There are two optional vignettes, but a length-eight route can contain only one. The two endings cover a viable biscuit gift and a sincere fallback note; they do not model every possible family response. The reference story is a longer authored narrative, not a promise that every reference beat appears in every generated route. A compatible route and a valid trace do not prove literary quality or broad semantic diversity.
